From: Emma Torres <emma@pinegrove.ai>

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial sizing info + context examples (Pinegrove)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — team was excited by the latency and cost controls. We need to get model selection and rough sizing nailed down so our SRE and procurement teams can move in parallel. A few details from our side: 

- Primary feature: real-time document summarization + Q&A for long-form customer reports (avg doc length ~18k chars).
- Typical request pattern: 1–3 calls per customer session, 80% of sessions are single-call.
- Expected launch footprint: ~1K active sessions/day first month; expected ramp to 8K sessions/day over 3 months.
- Latency target: 95th <= 350ms for the shortest summaries; interactive Q&A can tolerate up to 800ms.
- Context: we want to preserve ~4k tokens of document context for extractive Q&A (most queries reference specific report sections).

I've attached a redacted sample payloads file and a short doc describing session patterns. Can you propose a 2–3 model shortlist and a ballpark token/day estimate (including both prompt + response tokens) for initial and ramp phases? Also let us know if prefix/KV caching is recommended for this workload.

Emma
Emma Torres
Product Ops, Pinegrove Analytics

Attachment: pinegrove_sample_payloads.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Torres <emma@pinegrove.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing info + context examples (Pinegrove)

Emma — thanks for the detail and sample payloads. This gives us a solid starting point. Below is a short, practical proposal so your SRE/procurement can proceed in parallel with CS/Implementation: 

Summary recommendation (shortlist):
- Candidate A: redwood-llama-large (quantized 8-bit) — best latency per cost, good for high-throughput summarization when you can accept slightly shorter response windows.
- Candidate B: redwood-llama-xl (FP16) — stronger long-context coherence, recommended if you want a higher-quality extractive Q&A experience at slightly higher cost.
- Candidate C: open-mix-13B (8-bit + KV cache optimizations) — good balance for document-heavy Q&A where KV prefix caching materially reduces repeated context recomputation.

Key sizing assumptions (ballpark):
- Average prompt tokens per call: 3,200 (includes 4k token context excerpt -> tokenized down to ~3.2k after preprocessing/cleanup).
- Average response tokens per call: 150 (concise answer/summary).
- Calls/day: initial 1,000 sessions * 1.2 calls/session = 1,200 calls/day; ramp 8,000 sessions * 1.3 calls/session = 10,400 calls/day.
- Token/day initial: (3,200 + 150) * 1,200 ≈ 4.02M tokens/day.
- Token/day ramp: (3,200 + 150) * 10,400 ≈ 34.82M tokens/day.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching: strongly recommended for Candidate C and B when customers re-query the same document across sessions (saves ~40–60% token compute in real workloads). For Candidate A, gains are smaller because it's optimized for low-latency single-pass summaries.
- Batching: configure short batching window (10–15ms) for summarization paths to improve throughput without impacting 95th latency SLO.
- Quantization: 8-bit quantization is sensible for Candidate A and C; choose FP16 for Candidate B if you prioritize quality.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether the 4k token context is strict or if you can accept a trimmed 3k working window for cheaper latency.
2) If you want, we can run a 48-hour sample run on Redwood Dedicated (small pool) to get measured p95 latency and precise token-costs — CS and SRE find that data most useful for procurement.

I'll leave Grace and Connor on copy to propose a minimal Dedicated config and an initial Dedicated quote for the size above.

Best,
Rafael
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this is super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 4k token context is our target for extractive QA; for the fast summary path we can reduce the context to 2k. We want the system to support both flows.
- We expect heavy locality: the same document will be queried multiple times across a session, so KV caching should give us real wins.
- Procurement wants a measured cost estimate for the first-month launch (1k sessions/day) including an optional Dedicated pool for the first 2 months.

Grace / Connor — forwarding Pinegrove's context and OK to run the 48-hour Dedicated sample. Quick internal plan below (high level, please confirm):

1) Dedicated pool proposal: start with 2x A100-equivalent nodes (fp16 + 8-bit friendly), allow burstable + autoscale to 3 nodes during peak. This maps to our expected initial volume (~4M tokens/day) with comfortably low p95 for Candidate A and Candidate C.
2) Runtime config: enable KV prefix caching with 12 hour TTL for document objects; short batching window (12ms) for summaries, slightly longer (20ms) for Q&A.
3) Telemetry capture: capture per-token latency breakdown, cache hit/miss rate, and token counters during the 48-hour run; share a dashboard link with Pinegrove at 24h / 48h.
4) Quote: Connor — can you draft a preliminary Dedicated quote (monthly pro-rate for first 2 months) and include estimated token unit spend using Rafael's numbers?
5) Legal/Procurement: Rafael — I'll push the SLA draft and NDA to Legal; Emma attached them already.

Anything I'm missing? If we agree, I'll book the Dedicated pool for Tue morning PST and coordinate a handoff call with CS for measurement interpretation.

— Rafael
